Lemma
[Leibniz rule for the fixed metric at $p$]

1. ch3:4.1For curves $f,h:\mathbb {R}\to T_pM$ differentiable at $t$, read in the chart at $p$, \[ \frac{d}{dt}\langle f(t),h(t)\rangle _p = \langle f'(t),h(t)\rangle _p + \langle f(t),h'(t)\rangle _p. \]
Proof

\sketch

The form is the finite sum $\sum _{i,j}G_{ij}\, f^i(t)\, h^j(t)$ with constant coefficients $G_{ij}$ (the base point is fixed); each coordinate $f^i,h^j$ is a continuous linear functional of the curve, so the product rule applies termwise.

□
